source.check: the five divisions and names read from the News-Letter's 'Down local elections' report (27 April 1933, p. 16), which states that there were no nominations for the other eleven divisions

note: Triennial election of the rural district councillors. Nominations were received by Mr. S. J. Crail at the Lisburn Union offices on 26 April 1933. Five divisions were nominated; there were no nominations for the other eleven, whose sitting members were automatically returned. Polling in County Down took place on 25 May 1933. Filed on 1933-05-25, the polling day for county council and rural district elections in Co. Down that year (confirmed); previously filed under 1933-06-01 (verification 5 Nov 2026). Seven of the eleven sitting members returned without nomination are recorded from Lisburn Standard reports of the council's meetings (30 May - 14 November 1933); Glassdrummond fell vacant by the death of R. C. Martin and T. B. Morrow was co-opted (not an election); Ballyskeagh (A. A. Gillespie, co-opted for it in 1931) and Breda (James Dick, co-opted for it in 1927) are added from the meetings of 30 May and 11 July 1933 (round 2, 7 Nov 2026); Drumbo remains unnamed (meetings pass, 7 Nov 2026). Returned unopposed.
